explanation: Count inversions while merge-sorting a copy. When the next right-half value precedes a left-half value, it is smaller than every remaining left-half value, contributing middle−i inversions. Equal values are taken from the left and do not count.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: Recursive calls count inversions within each half. During merge, when a right value is smaller than the current left value, it is smaller than every remaining left value, contributing exactly that remaining count. Every inversion belongs to exactly one of these categories.
walkthrough: For [3,1,2,1], the first 3 exceeds the three later values, giving three inversions. The 2 exceeds the final 1, giving one more. The total is 4.
edgeCases: Counting uses original index order before merge sorting.
